method: MIXED, THREE SOURCE FAMILIES, EACH USED FOR WHAT IT COVERS. C1-C5 are five AMH pages, paraphrased, no passage stored: they carry the DRUG LADDER and the DOSES. S1 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP article on acute severe ulcerative colitis (April 2024), quoted verbatim: it carries SEVERITY CRITERIA, SURGICAL THRESHOLDS AND POSTOPERATIVE COMPLICATION RATES, none of which AMH provides. S2 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP article on perinatal IBD management (October 2022 -- FOUR YEARS OLD, stated in the guideline), quoted verbatim: it carries PRECONCEPTION, ANTENATAL AND POSTPARTUM DETAIL where AMH says only 'seek specialist advice'. This guideline closes TWO AMH topics (Crohn's disease, Ulcerative colitis). Where the sources agree -- sulfasalazine and male fertility, methotrexate and the 3-month rule -- the agreement is recorded as agreement.

claims.claim: Budesonide capsules and tablets must be swallowed whole and not crushed or chewed, and treatment must not be stopped suddenly; Budenofalk capsules may be opened and the contents swallowed whole with a glass of water if the patient cannot swallow them
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Budesonide' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/gastrointestinal-drugs/drugs-inflammatory-bowel-disease/corticosteroids-gastrointestinal/budesonide, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Budesonide' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/gastrointestinal-drugs/drugs-inflammatory-bowel-disease/corticosteroids-gastrointestinal/budesonide, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CORTIMENT, the 9 mg controlled-release budesonide tablet for ulcerative colitis, is listed by AMH with NO PBS listing, while the Crohn's disease capsules and the rectal foam are PBS-listed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Budesonide' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/gastrointestinal-drugs/drugs-inflammatory-bowel-disease/corticosteroids-gastrointestinal/budesonide, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: In 2021 ulcerative colitis patients were estimated to account for 334 out of every 100,000 patients presenting to general practitioners in Australia, and ACUTE SEVERE ULCERATIVE COLITIS is seen in UP TO 25% of that population, requiring swift and decisive emergency care
claims.source_text: In 2021, ulcerative colitis (UC) patients were estimated to account for 334 out of every 100,000 patients presenting to general practitioners (GPs) in Australia. … A severe complication, known as acute severe UC (ASUC), is seen in up to 25% of this population and requires swift and decisive emergency care to prevent further deterioration.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The TRUELOVE AND WITTS criteria are the most sensitive and prevalently used for defining acute severe ulcerative colitis from a surgical perspective; a patient typically has AT LEAST SIX BLOODY MOTIONS DAILY plus a minimum of one sign of systemic toxicity
claims.source_text: From a surgical perspective, the Truelove and Witts severity criteria is the most sensitive and prevalently used for defining ASUC. … A patient with ASUC typically exhibits at least six bloody motions daily and a minimum of one sign of systemic toxicity
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The Truelove and Witts criteria are bloody stools more than 6 per day PLUS ONE OF: tachycardia with heart rate above 90 beats/min, pyrexia with core temperature above 37.8 degrees Celsius, raised inflammatory markers with ESR above 30 mm/h or CRP above 30 mg/L, or low haemoglobin below 10.5 g/dL
claims.source_text: Bloody stools >6 per day Plus one of Tachycardia Heart rate >90 beats/min Pyrexia Core temperature >37.8 ° C Raised inflammatory markers ESR >30 mm/h CRP >30 mg/L Low haemoglobin Hb <10.5 g/dL
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Australian guidelines, based on the Montreal classification, stratify risk into mild with 4 or fewer stools without blood, moderate with more than 4 with or without blood, and severe with 6 or more stools with blood and signs of toxicity; whichever criteria are chosen, THE CLASSIFICATION OF SEVERITY REQUIRES PERIODIC RE-EVALUATION
claims.source_text: Australian guidelines, based on the Montreal classification, stratify risk into mild ( ≤ 4 stools without blood), moderate ( > 4 with or without blood) and severe (≥6 stools, with blood and signs of toxicity). … Regardless of the chosen criteria, the classification of severity requires periodic re-evaluation.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A screen for opportunistic infections -- HIV, hepatitis B and C, and varicella zoster -- WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE BE MASKED, should be conducted in preparation for rescue pharmacotherapy with infliximab or cyclosporin; if prior tuberculosis exposure is likely, an interferon-gamma release assay is recommended
claims.source_text: A screen for opportunistic infections (ie human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B and C and varicella zoster), which would otherwise be masked, should be conducted in preparation for rescue pharmaco-therapy (ie infliximab or cyclosporin). … If prior tuberculosis exposure is likely, performing an interferon-gamma release assay is recommended
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Rescue therapy is typically used as SECOND-LINE treatment when intravenous steroid therapy fails to manage the disease over a span of THREE TO FIVE DAYS; serum magnesium and lipid profiles may also be arranged in preparation for cyclosporin
claims.source_text: Typically, rescue therapy is used as a second-line treatment when intravenous steroid therapy fails to manage the disease over a span of three to five days. … Serum magnesium levels and lipid profiles might also be arranged in preparation for cyclosporin treatment.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: STOOL TESTING TO EXCLUDE AN INFECTIVE CAUSE IS INDICATED, and a faecal calprotectin assay can assess disease severity, with a level above 50 mcg/g possibly representing active inflammation
claims.source_text: Stool testing, to exclude an infective cause, is also indicated. … Additionally, a faecal calprotectin assay can assess disease severity; a calprotectin level >50 mcg/g might represent active inflammation.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Abdominal radiography is used to identify TOXIC MEGACOLON, and gas-less prep-less sigmoidoscopy should be performed at the earliest opportunity -- studies show improved outcomes in patients undergoing endoscopy WITHIN 72 HOURS of hospitalisation
claims.source_text: Diagnostic imaging, including abdominal radiography, is used to identify toxic megacolon. … It should be performed at the earliest opportunity, with various studies demonstrating improved outcomes in ASUC patients undertaking endoscopy within 72 hours of hospitalisation.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Initial medical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis is intravenous glucocorticoids with potential escalation to a biologic agent, usually infliximab, AIMING TO REDUCE COLECTOMY RATES BY UP TO 80%
claims.source_text: Initial medical management includes intravenous glucocorticoids with potential escalation to a biologic agent (usually infliximab) … and aims to reduce colectomy rates by up to 80%.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Medications carrying a potential risk of inducing COLONIC DILATATION should be used cautiously in acute severe ulcerative colitis -- anticholinergics, antidiarrhoeals and opiates
claims.source_text: Medications that harbour a potential risk of inducing colonic dilatation should be used cautiously (eg anticholinergics, antidiarrheals and opiates).
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A recent randomised trial concluded that the use of ANTIBIOTICS in acute severe ulcerative colitis DID NOT IMPROVE OUTCOMES outside a clinical context of severe sepsis
claims.source_text: a recent randomised trial concluded that the use of antibiotics in ASUC did not improve outcomes outside a clinical context of severe sepsis
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients with acute severe ulcerative colitis have an UP TO EIGHT-FOLD INCREASED RISK OF THROMBOEMBOLISM, so compression stockings and chemical thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight or unfractionated heparin are usually prescribed
claims.source_text: ASUC patients have an up to eight-fold increased risk of thromboembolism because of prolonged hospitalisation, convalescence and the systemic burden of a profound inflammatory process. … Therefore, compression stockings and chemical thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight or unfractionated heparin are usually prescribed.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Increased risk of POST-DISCHARGE venous thromboembolism is identified in patients aged 45 years and older, with a hospital stay of seven days or longer, and with a previous history of C. difficile infection on initial admission
claims.source_text: Patients aged 45 years and older, who have a hospital stay of seven days or longer, and with a previous history of C. difficile infection upon their initial admission are identified as having an increased risk for post-discharge venous thromboembolism (VTE).
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Complications requiring IMMEDIATE surgical intervention are TOXIC MEGACOLON, HAEMATOCHEZIA WITH HAEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY, and PERFORATION
claims.source_text: Such complications encompass toxic megacolon, haematochezia paired with haemodynamic instability, and perforation.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The TRAVIS CRITERIA can help predict surgical need, particularly if a patient has MORE THAN EIGHT DAILY STOOLS, or THREE TO EIGHT STOOLS WITH A CRP ABOVE 45 mg/L, AFTER THREE DAYS ON STEROIDS
claims.source_text: The Travis criteria can help predict surgical need, particularly if a patient has more than eight daily stools or three to eight stools with a C-reactive protein level above 45mg/L after three days on steroids.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Common indications for ELECTIVE surgery in ulcerative colitis are the INABILITY TO WEAN OFF STEROIDS or the presence of DYSPLASIA
claims.source_text: Common indications include the inability to wean off steroids or the presence of dysplasia.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Urgent and emergency patients typically undergo a TOTAL ABDOMINAL COLECTOMY AND END ILEOSTOMY, while elective patients are often offered restorative techniques, most commonly an ILEAL POUCH ANAL ANASTOMOSIS
claims.source_text: Urgent and emergency patients typically undergo a total abdominal colectomy and end ileostomy. In contrast, elective patients are often presented with restorative techniques, most commonly an ileal pouch anal anastomosis.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Postoperative complication rates a GP should know: ANASTOMOTIC STRICTURE in 4 to 16% of cases, identifiable on per rectal examination; BOWEL OBSTRUCTION in 2 to 4%; and PELVIC SEPSIS AND POUCH FAILURE in 8.5 to 9.5%
claims.source_text: GPs might identify an anastomotic stricture, occurring in 4-16% of cases, during a per rectal examination. … If a patient exhibits symptoms of bowel obstruction (2-4%), GPs should prioritise cross-sectional imaging and promptly refer to the surgical team. … GPs should be vigilant for signs of pelvic sepsis and pouch failure, found in 8.5-9.5% of patients.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IMMEDIATE referral to the emergency department is vital for patients showing infective symptoms, heightened faecal frequency of MORE THAN FOUR TO SIX BOWEL MOTIONS A DAY, loose stools, or symptoms of obstruction
claims.source_text: Immediate referral to the emergency department is vital for patients showing infective symptoms, heightened faecal frequency (ie more than four to six bowel motions a day), loose stools or symptoms of obstruction.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Faecal incontinence and overnight incontinence are COMMON after pouch surgery, in 53 to 76% of patients, who present with an average of six daily stools or an overnight stool
claims.source_text: Faecal incontinence and overnight incontinence are common symptoms in patients who have undergone pouch surgery (53-76%), with patients presenting with an average of six daily stools or an overnight stool.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Sexual outcomes after surgery: in male patients IMPOTENCE in 1.5% or RETROGRADE EJACULATION in 4%; in female patients temporary DYSPAREUNIA in 7%, with frequency of intercourse and capacity to achieve orgasm usually unchanged; and approximately 88% of female patients who have had a surgical intervention and hope to conceive have successfully given birth
claims.source_text: For male patients, sexual dysfunction might manifest as impotence (1.5%) or retrograde ejaculation (4%). … In female patients, while some might temporarily grapple with dyspareunia (7%), their frequency of intercourse and capacity to achieve orgasm usually remain unchanged. … approximately 88% of female patients who have undergone a surgical intervention and hoping to conceive have successfully given birth
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Identification and surgical management of acute severe ulcerative colitis', Volume 53 Issue 4, April 2024, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2024/april/identification-and-surgical-management-of-acute-se, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AUSTRALIA HAS ONE OF THE HIGHEST RATES OF IBD IN THE WORLD, with a prevalence of more than one in 300; more than 50% of patients are diagnosed before 35 years of age and more than 25% of affected women conceive for the first time after their IBD diagnosis
claims.source_text: Australia has one of the highest rates of IBD in the world, with a prevalence of more than one in 300. … Greater than 50% of patients are diagnosed with IBD prior to 35 years of age, and more than 25% of affected women conceive for the first time following their IBD diagnosis.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: UP TO ONE-THIRD OF PATIENTS WITH IBD ARE MANAGED EXCLUSIVELY BY A PRIMARY CARE PHYSICIAN
claims.source_text: up to one-third of patients with IBD are managed exclusively by a primary care physician
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Disease flares occur in between 20% and 55% of patients with IBD antenatally
claims.source_text: disease flares occurring in between 20% and 55% of patients antenatally
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Compared with those in remission, patients with ACTIVE IBD in pregnancy have a GREATER THAN THREE-FOLD INCREASED RISK of spontaneous abortion, low birth weight infants and preterm delivery, and an increased risk of stillbirths
claims.source_text: Compared with those in remission, patients with active IBD in pregnancy have a greater than three-fold increased risk of spontaneous abortion, low birth weight infants and preterm delivery, as well as an increased risk of stillbirths.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Of those in clinical remission, approximately ONE-THIRD will experience a flare in pregnancy, compared with 55% OF THOSE WITH ACTIVE DISEASE AT THE TIME OF CONCEPTION; THREE MONTHS OF CORTICOSTEROID-FREE clinical and biochemical, cross-sectional imaging or endoscopic remission is recommended before attempting conception
claims.source_text: Of those in clinical remission, approximately one-third will experience a flare in pregnancy, compared with 55% of those with active disease at the time of conception. … Thus, three months of corticosteroid-free clinical and biochemical, cross-sectional imaging or endoscopic remission is recommended prior to attempting conception.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Folate: 2 TO 5 mg DAILY is needed in extensive ileal disease, on a fibre-restricted diet, and in those taking SULFASALAZINE, for three months prior to conception and in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy
claims.source_text: 2-5 mg daily of folate is needed in the setting of extensive ileal disease, in those on a fibre-restricted diet and in those taking sulfasalazine for three months prior to conception and in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Weight: with a BMI above 30, a 5 to 10% body weight reduction before conception decreases the risk of adverse obstetric outcomes such as stillbirth
claims.source_text: BMI >30 kg/m 2 : 5-10% body weight reduction prior to conception in order to decrease the risk of adverse obstetric outcomes such as stillbirth.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CONTRACEPTION IN IBD: prefer long-acting, NON-OESTROGEN containing contraception in active IBD given the theoretical risk of venous thromboembolism; absorption of oral contraceptives is maintained in mild ulcerative colitis or short ileal resections; and non-oral contraceptives are recommended after extensive small bowel resection or with active small bowel inflammatory disease
claims.source_text: Preference for long-acting, non-oestrogen containing contraception in patients with active IBD, given the theoretical risk of venous thromboembolism. … Reassurance that absorption of oral contraceptives is maintained in those with mild UC or short ileal resections. … Recommendation for non-oral contraceptives in the setting of prior extensive small bowel resection or active small bowel inflammatory disease.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: LIVE VACCINATION with MMR in immunosuppressed patients receiving thiopurines, biologics or long-term corticosteroids must be tailored to the individual risk profile WITH INFECTIOUS DISEASE SPECIALIST INPUT
claims.source_text: Live vaccination (MMR) in immunosuppressed patients (receiving thiopurines, biologics or corticosteroids long term) must be tailored to individual risk profile with infectious disease specialist input.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: HEREDITABILITY IS REASSURINGLY LOW: the risk of IBD developing in a child born to a mother with IBD is approximately 1.6 to 4.1% for ulcerative colitis and 2.7 to 4.8% for Crohn's disease, varying by ethnicity -- but as high as 30% WHERE BOTH PARENTS ARE AFFECTED
claims.source_text: The risk of IBD developing in a child born to a mother with IBD varies according to ethnicity but is reassuringly low at approximately 1.6-4.1% for UC and between 2.7% and 4.8% for CD. … IBD risk can be as high as 30% in those with both parents affected by IBD.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Fertility does not appear to be adversely affected in women with WELL-CONTROLLED IBD, but may be decreased with severely active or complex penetrating disease, extensive prior surgical resections, or low BMI; refer for fertility specialist review within 6 to 12 months of unsuccessful attempts at conception, particularly after prior surgery
claims.source_text: Fertility does not appear to be adversely affected in women with well-controlled IBD but may be decreased in the setting of severely active or complex penetrating disease, as well as in those with extensive prior surgical resections or low body mass index (BMI). … Referral for fertility specialist review should be considered within 6-12 months of unsuccessful attempts at conception, particularly in those with prior surgical interventions.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Thiopurine metabolites, 6-thioguanine and 6-methylmercaptopurine, should be checked prior to conception and monitored throughout pregnancy because of the associated increased risk of INTRAHEPATIC CHOLESTASIS OF PREGNANCY
claims.source_text: thiopurine metabolites (6-thioguanine and 6-methylmercaptopurine) should be checked prior to conception and monitored throughout pregnancy because of the associated increased risk of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: BIOLOGIC MEDICATIONS SHOULD BE CONTINUED THROUGHOUT CONCEPTION AND PREGNANCY
claims.source_text: Biologic medications should be continued throughout conception and pregnancy
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Assessment in EACH TRIMESTER is recommended, INCLUDING IN THOSE IN REMISSION; biochemical assessment matters particularly because symptoms of active IBD are difficult to distinguish from other pregnancy complications, and ROUTINE INFLAMMATORY MARKERS ARE AFFECTED BY PREGNANCY and must be interpreted against pregnancy reference ranges
claims.source_text: Assessment in each trimester, including in those in remission, is recommended. … routine inflammatory markers are affected by pregnancy and must be interpreted with consideration for appropriate pregnancy reference ranges
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: FAECAL CALPROTECTIN REMAINS ACCURATE IN PREGNANCY and can also be used to evaluate symptoms potentially attributable to new-onset IBD such as rectal bleeding and diarrhoea; a level of 50 micrograms/g or more should prompt expedient gastroenterological referral for consideration of endoscopy or imaging
claims.source_text: Contrastingly, faecal calprotectin remains accurate in pregnancy and can additionally be used to evaluate those with symptoms potentially attributable to new-onset IBD, such as rectal bleeding and diarrhoea. … a faecal calprotectin ≥50 μg/g should prompt expedient gastroenterological referral for consideration of endoscopy or imaging
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A faecal calprotectin above 250 micrograms/g in pregnancy is associated with increased risks of adverse obstetric outcomes IRRESPECTIVE OF CLINICAL SYMPTOMS; measure it at least once in each trimester including in clinical remission, and a level above 250 requires consideration of therapeutic escalation and early gastroenterological review
claims.source_text: A faecal calprotectin of >250 μg/g in pregnancy is associated with increased risks of adverse obstetric outcomes irrespective of clinical symptoms. … Faecal calprotectin should be measured at least once in each trimester, including in those in clinical remission. A faecal calprotectin >250 μg/g requires consideration of therapeutic escalation and early gastroenterological review.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'Preconception, antenatal and postpartum management of inflammatory bowel disease', Volume 51 Issue 10, October 2022, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2022/october/perinatal-management-of-inflammatory-bowel-disease, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMINOSALICYLATES AND MALE FERTILITY: switch to an alternative THREE MONTHS PRIOR to conception attempts; in female fertility and pregnancy, continue but use 5 mg daily of folic acid with sulfasalazine, and AVOID SULFASALAZINE IN BREASTFEEDING
